clue.text: Light work around the house?

parts.note: read as the design and arrangement of the windows that let light into a building, not easy household chores

explanation.surface: A request for some easy chores to do at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light work' looks like gentle tasks, but here it is the work of letting in light: the planned placing of windows in a building.
explanation.definitionFit: This architectural term covers the arrangement of windows and openings in a building's design.

clue.text: Regret switching continent for a bigger area

indicators.note: switching its direction tells us the word for regret is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: to regret something is to rue it
Asia is a continent

explanation.surface: Someone sorry to swap one continent for a larger region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching' turns the regret word round. 'a bigger area' is fair: the combined landmass is larger than the continent named in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The joined landmass of Europe and Asia covers a larger region than either continent by itself.

clue.text: Game, say, without one dropped service

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters wrap round the rest

parts.note: say, as in 'for example', abbreviates to e.g.

indicators.note: dropped tells us the letter for one is let fall from the word for game

parts.note: venison is game, meat from deer
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A game played short of one player who has been sent off from service.
explanation.walkthrough: Game here is meat, not a match; 'one dropped' removes the I, and 'without' is the old sense of outside, so the 'say' letters wrap the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the evening prayer service of the Anglican church, also called vespers.

clue.text: International banker

definitions.meaning: an international cricket or rugby match
crosswords call a river a banker because it has banks; a river in Hampshire

explanation.walkthrough: THE TEST is a famous trout river in Hampshire, England; 'banker' is the crossword word for anything with banks, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An international cricket fixture is a Test match, and a 'banker' is a river, here the Hampshire chalk stream of that name.

clue.text: Book about church success with oriental designers

indicators.note: about means going round, so the book's letters surround the others

parts.note: Acts is a book of the New Testament
RC stands for Roman Catholic, a church
a hit is a success
oriental means eastern, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A book on how a church prospered with help from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the church, success and oriental letters inside the book, which splits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: These professionals draw up plans for buildings, so they are designers.

clue.text: Popular bar's main branch

parts.note: popular things are in
a let is a hindrance or bar, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A well-liked pub is the chief outlet of a chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the sea, as in the Spanish Main, so a 'main branch' is an arm of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow arm of the sea reaching into the land is a branch of the main, the ocean.

clue.text: Poorer girl once known as first queen

indicators.note: first says the piece for once known as comes at the front, before the girl's name

parts.note: née introduces the name someone was known by before marriage
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
ER is Elizabeth Regina, a queen

explanation.surface: A poor girl who was formerly known as the first queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts NEE ahead of DI, though the clue mentions the girl first.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone more in want than another is worse off, in greater need.

clue.text: Painting technique in which print is made initially

parts.note: an impression is a print, as of a stamp or engraving

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word made is taken

explanation.surface: A painting method in which a print is created first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes M from 'made'; 'in which' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Monet and Renoir's movement painted fleeting light with loose brushwork, a style of painting.

clue.text: Political organiser who knows where to draw the line

definitions.text: Political organiser who knows where to draw the line

parts.words: Political organiser who knows where to draw the line
parts.note: read as a person who redraws electoral boundaries for party advantage, not someone with good judgement about limits

explanation.surface: A sensible party worker who knows the limits of acceptable behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw the line' usually means setting a moral limit; here it is literal, drawing constituency boundaries to rig an election.
explanation.definitionFit: This person manipulates electoral district boundaries to favour one party.

clue.text: Mushrooms originally served in very small portions

indicators.note: in tells us the first letter is placed inside the word for mushrooms

parts.note: morels are edible mushrooms

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of served is taken

explanation.surface: Mushrooms first served up in tiny helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives S from 'served', which goes 'in' MORELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny pieces or mouthfuls of food are small portions.

clue.text: Member takes old king around school

indicators.note: around tells us the old king's name is put round the limb

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry old king of the nursery rhyme
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A club member takes an old monarch on a tour of a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the container signal; 'takes' only links. The nursery-rhyme king is the crossword's usual old king.
explanation.definitionFit: A school can be a place of higher learning or a private secondary institution such as Eton.

clue.text: Financial arrangements not root of plants' problems

indicators.note: not root tells us to drop the start, the root, of the word for financial arrangements

parts.note: trusts are legal arrangements for holding money and property

explanation.surface: Money matters that are not at the heart of a gardener's troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUSTS loses its first letter, its 'root', to leave RUSTS; 'of' links. 'root of plants' looks like one phrase, but 'plants' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust is a fungal disease that attacks leaves and stems, so these are ailments of vegetation.

clue.text: More disgusting if arranged with Hitler

indicators.note: arranged tells us the letters of the two words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Things get nastier if a plan is made with Hitler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles IF and HITLER together; 'with' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dirtier or more obscene is more repellent.

clue.text: Follow cockney woman's pet hound

parts.note: to track someone is to follow them
a cockney drops the h, so her becomes 'er
a dog is a typical pet

explanation.surface: Trailing a Londoner's beloved hunting dog.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockney is a working-class Londoner, whose accent drops the initial H, so 'her' is said as 'ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog trained to follow a scent is a kind of hunting hound.

clue.text: Asians rent out Cornish areas

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the two words are put out of order

explanation.surface: Asian landlords letting out property in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles ASIANS and RENT. Cornwall is a county in southwest England, once famous for tin mining.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the tin-mining districts of Cornwall and Devon, with their own courts and laws.

clue.text: Frenchman comes back to study

indicators.note: comes back means the French name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Marc is a French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman returns to his books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back' turns MARC round.
explanation.definitionFit: To study hard and fast before an exam is to swot intensively.

clue.text: Terrier's leash may get tangled

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: may get tangled tells us the letters of the lead and the following word are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: A small dog's lead could become knotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may get tangled' shuffles LEASH and MAY, though 'may' reads as part of the indicator. The definition's 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Welsh breed is a short-legged, wiry white terrier.

clue.text: Schemer rejecting first class game

indicators.note: rejecting means turning back, so the letters for first class are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first class, read here as the letters A and I
Go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A plotter refusing an elite contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns A1 round, with the numeral 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's villain in Othello is the classic plotter, who engineers the hero's downfall.

clue.text: Doctor blows out and takes a chance

indicators.note: out means outside, so the word for blows sits outside the doctor

parts.note: gales are strong winds, blows
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A medic puffs out his cheeks and decides to risk it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' means outside here; 'and' only links. 'blows' looks like a verb but stands for strong winds.
explanation.definitionFit: To bet or risk something on an uncertain outcome is to gamble.

clue.text: Weapon cut strange characters

indicators.note: characters means letters, here the letters of the words before taken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A weapon used to cut down odd-looking people.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters ('characters') of CUT STRANGE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun firing a wide spread of shot is a firearm.

clue.text: Dress to look older? Nonsense!

parts.note: garb is clothing, dress
to age is to grow or appear older

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of dressing to seem older.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish or drivel, talk without sense, is a common exclamation of disbelief.

clue.text: Limited company takes on journalist

indicators.note: takes on means the company word adds the journalist after it

parts.note: a number is a company or group, as in 'one of our number'
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A limited company hires a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limited' looks like part of 'Limited company'; it is the definition, as in 'your days are numbered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are few or restricted in quantity are counted, so finite.

clue.text: Organise party odds on ERM scheme

indicators.note: odds on means the odd-placed letters across the two words are taken

explanation.surface: Arranging a celebration with a bet on a European currency plan.
explanation.walkthrough: ERM was the European Exchange Rate Mechanism; the odd letters of ERM SCHEME give E, M, C, E, E.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as master of ceremonies, an MC, is to host or compere an event.

clue.text: Great liberty

definitions.meaning: a prisoner on the loose is 'at ...', at liberty

explanation.definitionFit: Big in size is one sense; free, as in an escaped convict being 'at large', is the other.

clue.text: No space to grow this soft pulp

indicators.note: no tells us the word for space is removed from the word for grow

parts.note: to mushroom is to grow rapidly
room is space

explanation.surface: Without enough room, this soft mass cannot develop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'this' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft, wet, pulpy mass, such as porridge, is a mash.

clue.text: Page cut out and joined

indicators.note: out means outside, so the word for cut sits around the page letter

parts.note: sliced means cut

explanation.surface: A page was cut out and stuck together again.
explanation.walkthrough: SLICED goes 'out', round P; 'and' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropes or film joined end to end are spliced together.

clue.text: Lift ambassador in cheerful way

indicators.note: in tells us the ambassador goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: up means cheerful
Ave is short for avenue, a way
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: Raising a diplomat high in a happy manner.
explanation.walkthrough: HE goes 'in' UP + AVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave up something is to raise it.

clue.text: Tool giving advantage to husband in prison

indicators.note: in tells us the advantage and husband go inside the prison

parts.note: slammer is slang for prison
an edge is an advantage

explanation.surface: A tool gives a husband the upper hand in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: EDGE and H go 'in' SLAMMER; 'giving' links.
explanation.definitionFit: This heavy long-handled hammer is a tool for breaking stone.
